newsitem.title: LEBANON: Strongest quake in 40 years rocks Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Strongest quake in 40 years rocks Lebanon.

text.p: An earthquake and several aftershocks rocked Lebanon on Wednesday, swaying building and causing slight damage, and a seismologist said the tremor was the strongest felt in the country in 40 years.

Damage was slight and there were no injuries but some residents compared the first short, sharp shock at 6:22 a.m. (0422 GMT), which measured 5.5 on the Richter scale, with a 1956 earthquake that flattened buildings and whole villages.
"My bed rocked heavily. I don't recall being that frightened since the big 1956 earthquake," a housewife in the southern city of Sidon said.
The quake was also felt in Israel where it shook buildings in Haifa and Tel Aviv.

Lebanese police said cracks appeared in old buildings in Beirut. Masonry fell from a few houses in the capital and residents said pictures fell from walls and vases and other objects fell to the floor.
Another 15-second tremor measuring 4.3 on the Richter scale struck nine hours later, again shaking buildings strongly across the country.
"It was an aftershock, preceded by 10 smaller ones with magnitudes ranging between 2.5 and 3.5 on the Richter scale," Charles Thabet of the state-run Bhannes Seismological Centre, told Reuters.
The epicentre of the quake was in the eastern Mediterranean 135 km (85 miles) northwest of Beirut, Thabet said.
A tremor measuring 5.7 on the Richter scale shook Lebanon on January 22 but was not felt as strongly as Wednesday's tremors because its epicentre was further from the country.
"What makes today's earthquake stronger than January's and all the others since 1956 is that its epicentre was closer to Lebanon," Thabet said.
The 1956 quake measured six on the Richter scale.
